chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Al-Jalal ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Al-'Ala' ibn Ra'ab from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
The divorced woman performs Hajj and testifies for the rights.
ai.seo_question: Can a divorced woman perform Hajj and settle her rights?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the legal capacity of a divorced woman (mutallaqah) to perform Hajj and settle her financial dues, reflecting the Shia view that divorce does not restrict her religious agency. Scholars note that 'shahada al-huquq' implies she must ensure her mahr and waiting period (iddah) obligations are clear, allowing her to travel without hindrance from her ex-husband. This ruling underscores the balance between personal religious duty and financial accountability in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazan, and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al A’la, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The divorced woman can perform Hajj, and testify for the rights’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al- Jabbar from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A divorced woman can perform al-Hajj and testify about rights.’”
